item.title: Kadavu celebrates first Skipper, Marama wins at home
item.description: KADAVU gave their home supporters plenty to celebrate on Saturday, recording their first victories of the Skipper Cup season with a clean sweep against Rewa. Kadavu won all three matches, with the Under-20 side getting the day off to a winning start before the Marama Championship team followed suit.
item.content:encoded:
KADAVU gave their home supporters plenty to celebrate on Saturday, recording their first victories of the Skipper Cup season with a clean sweep against Rewa.

Kadavu won all three matches, with the Under-20 side getting the day off to a winning start before the Marama Championship team followed suit.

The senior men then completed the clean sweep with a victory over Rewa, making it a memorable day for the province.

It was the first of four home rounds for Kadavu, giving the young union an encouraging start to its home campaign. Kadavu Rugby Union president Lynda Tabuya described the occasion as a significant moment for the province.

“This is such a historic day for Kadavu,” Tabuya said.

Kadavu’s rugby union was established only about three years ago through the Bose ni Vanua at the Kadavu Provincial Council.

“We only formed not only three years ago, and we were formed by the Bose Vanua at the Kadavu Provincial Council, so we are really provincial based,” she said.

Tabuya said Kadavu was still establishing itself among Fiji’s provincial rugby unions.

“We are the newest kids on the block,” she said.

The first wins of the season were made even more special by the support from the Kadavu community, which turned out to back the teams.

“I just thank the Vanua and the people of Kadavu for rallying the behind the Kadavu team,” Tabuya said.

The three victories provide Kadavu with a much-needed boost after its opening matches and give the players confidence heading into the next round. With three more home rounds to come, Kadavu will now look to build on its first taste of victory and continue growing as a provincial rugby union.

item.title: Mannu: Rewa ready to embrace biggest test yet
item.description: REWA FC heads into tomorrow’s OFC Men’s Champions League semi-final against Auckland City with growing belief, as the Fijian side looks to turn its recent momentum into a place in the final. The semi-final kicks off at 3pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, with Rewa facing one of the region’s most experienced sides.
item.content:encoded:
REWA FC heads into tomorrow’s OFC Men’s Champions League semi-final against Auckland City with growing belief, as the Fijian side looks to turn its recent momentum into a place in the final.

The semi-final kicks off at 3pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, with Rewa facing one of the region’s most experienced sides.

For Rewa assistant coach Priyant Mannu, the team’s journey through the tournament has already shown the character within the squad.

“After the opening match, the result was not in our favour, but after that the boys picked up and we had to fight to move on,” Mannu said.

He believes Rewa has grown stronger with every match and is beginning to find its rhythm at the right time.

“As you can see in the past two games, we have been at crucial points, but we managed to get it. Looking forward, I think the boys are gaining momentum as the game goes along,” he said.

That confidence will be important against Auckland City, but Mannu believes Rewa has prepared for the challenge and will focus on what it can control.

“They have been winning this for the past year, so it’s a little bit tough for us, but we do have a plan,” he said.

For Mannu, composure will be one of the keys to Rewa’s chances.

“Our main focus will be staying composed throughout the 90 minutes,” he said.

While the occasion is bigger, Mannu said the team has maintained its preparation and approach.

“For us, it’s really been the same,” he said.

The difference is that Wednesday offers no second opportunity.

“We know there’s no second chance. If we lose, we go out, and if we win, we can reach the final and get closer to our goal,” Mannu said.

He believes the entire Rewa camp is ready for the challenge.

“All the boys are ready to take on Auckland City on Wednesday,” he said.

For Rewa, a victory would be more than a place in the final.

“It will be a proud moment for Fiji, a milestone achievement for the team in the Fiji region finals,” Mannu said.

With belief growing and the final within reach, Rewa now has 90 minutes to make its opportunity count.

item.title: ‘Fiji’s grassroots rugby inspiring’
item.description: SOUTH Africa Women’s rugby captain Babalwa Latsha has been impressed by Fiji’s deep-rooted rugby culture after witnessing the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Rugby Championship over the past two weeks. Latsha, who led the South African side to a 29-22 victory over the Vodafone Fijiana XV at Churchill Park on Saturday, said the passion for rugby among young Fijians was unlike anything she had experi
item.content:encoded:
SOUTH Africa Women’s rugby captain Babalwa Latsha has been impressed by Fiji’s deep-rooted rugby culture after witnessing the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Rugby Championship over the past two weeks.

Latsha, who led the South African side to a 29-22 victory over the Vodafone Fijiana XV at Churchill Park on Saturday, said the passion for rugby among young Fijians was unlike anything she had experienced.

“Oh my goodness, my thoughts are that rugby in this country is contagious.

“You drive past on the buses and you see kids playing in the fields, and it’s a culture, it’s a spiritual thing, that’s what I’ve got from it,” Latsha said.

“And what better way as a nation to invest in the sport than to invest at grassroots level, right?

“Just let kids play as much as possible. It’s brilliant to see, and I can’t wait to see what Fijian rugby will look like in the next five to 10 years.”

Latsha said the experience had also given the South African team an appreciation of the warmth and hospitality of the Fijian people.

She said the similarities between the two nations’ cultures were evident throughout their stay.

South Africa’s victory secured the inaugural Ubuntu-Bula Trophy after the visitors also won the opening Test, giving them a 2-0 series sweep over the Fijiana XV.

item.title: Building the future
item.description: FOR the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association, the Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship is about more than trophies, results and competition. With 120 teams coming together from tomorrow to Friday at Jai Narayan College, the championship will give young players an opportunity to test themselves against schools from across the country while gaining valuable experience that could s
item.content:encoded:
FOR the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association, the Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship is about more than trophies, results and competition.

With 120 teams coming together from tomorrow to Friday at Jai Narayan College, the championship will give young players an opportunity to test themselves against schools from across the country while gaining valuable experience that could shape their future in the sport.

A total of 606 matches are scheduled across the three days, creating a busy programme for players, coaches, officials and supporters.

Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice-president Josua Qalo said the championship played an important role in developing the next generation of netballers.

“The Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship is more than just a tournament; it is a cornerstone for the future of netball in Fiji,” Qalo said.

He said bringing schools together helped strengthen grassroots development while creating a pathway for players to progress to district, national and international levels.

For young athletes, the championship is also an opportunity to develop qualities that extend beyond the court.

Qalo said competing at a national level teaches players discipline, teamwork, resilience and how to perform under pressure.

“These experiences prepare them for the demands of elite netball and instil confidence that extends beyond the court,” he said.

The three-day programme will feature competition across the Under-14, Under-15, Under-17, Under-19, Open and Boys divisions.

Defending champions will also face challenges across several grades, with Saint Joseph’s Secondary defending its Under-19 title, Holy Cross College aiming to retain the Open crown and Yat Sen Secondary returning to defend the Boys division.

Qalo said the Association had seen steady growth in participation, with more schools and students embracing netball.

He credited teachers, coaches and communities for helping create an environment where young players can develop and remain involved in the sport.

The growth of the championship also highlights the importance of sponsor support.

Qalo said Crest Chicken’s backing had helped the Association stage the competition on a national scale and create more opportunities for schools to participate.

“The sponsorship from Crest Chicken has been instrumental,” he said.

He said the partnership had helped reduce financial barriers while strengthening the profile of the championship.

Beyond the competition, Qalo hopes players leave with lessons that stay with them long after the final whistle.

He said sportsmanship, unity, respect, perseverance and leadership were just as important as technical skills.

For the Association, success will not be measured only by the final results.

“If our athletes leave motivated to continue their netball journey and our communities feel proud of the event, then we will consider the Championship a true success,” Qalo said.

With 120 teams and 606 matches ahead, the championship represents an important investment in the future of Fiji netball.

item.title: Redemption sends QVS into U16 final
item.description: Queen Victoria School’s under-16 team finally settled an old score with Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School when it edged the defending finalists in a tense Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Vodafone Super Deans Championship semi-final at Burchurst Park in Suva last Saturday. For QVS, the victory was about far more than securing a place in the final, it was redemption.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Victoria School’s under-16 team finally settled an old score with Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School when it edged the defending finalists in a tense Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Vodafone Super Deans Championship semi-final at Burchurst Park in Suva last Saturday.

For QVS, the victory was about far more than securing a place in the final, it was redemption.

The Vulinitu side had twice fallen to MGM in the knockout stages in recent years, first when the two sides met in the U14 grade and again last year in the U15 competition.

Technical coach Anare Sovanivalu said those defeats had remained part of the team’s journey and made Saturday’s breakthrough particularly significant.

“It was God that was with us in that match,” Sovanivalu said.

“We were coming in as underdogs because MGM were the finalists for last year.”

Sovanivalu said the players were well aware of the history between the two schools and the importance of finally overcoming their northern-zone rivals.

“When they were under-14, we lost to MGM in the quarter-finals. Last year, 2025, we again lost to MGM in the semi-finals,” he said.

“We were actually developing our boys and we’ve seen how it has grown. They have performed to what was expected.”

The victory has now taken the QVS U16 side one step further than last year and into the Super Deans final, where another formidable challenge awaits against Suva Grammar School.

Sovanivalu said QVS would again embrace the underdog tag.

“Suva Grammar is one of the finalists from last year. We are proud to come in as underdogs. We’ll give our all,” he said.

The coach believes the team has already achieved its primary development target this season, but winning the final would provide an even greater reward.

“Our target was to reach the final. Winning it will be a bonus but we will give it our absolute best,” he said.

The road to the final has also carried the weight of the wider QVS community, particularly after the school’s U18 side bowed out earlier in the competition.

Sovanivalu said the U16 players understood that they were now carrying the school’s hopes.

item.title: SVC targets national glory
item.description: SWAMI Vivekananda College will enter the Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship with three teams after an impressive showing at the Western Secondary Schools Netball Rally. The Nadi-based school secured qualification in the Under-14, Open Girls and Open Boys divisions, with the Under-14 and Open Girls finishing first while the Open Boys settled for third place.
item.content:encoded:
SWAMI Vivekananda College will enter the Crest Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championship with three teams after an impressive showing at the Western Secondary Schools Netball Rally.

The Nadi-based school secured qualification in the Under-14, Open Girls and Open Boys divisions, with the Under-14 and Open Girls finishing first while the Open Boys settled for third place.

Teacher-in-charge of netball, Mrs Laisa Tui, said it was an honour to have been involved with the school’s netball programme for the past five years and praised the support provided by the school administration.

The three teams comprise 36 players, with 12 players in each team, and Tui said they were ready for the national competition, which begins tomorrow at Jai Narayan College. Tui said the Open Men’s side was determined to improve on last year’s performance and finish among top three while the Open Girls team are also targeting a better finish after bowing out in the Cup semi-finals last year. However, the school’s excitement is centred on the Under-14 team as they will compete at the national level for the first time.

Tui said the young players had already caught the attention of the school with their performances and talents.

Despite a late Nadi Secondary Schools Netball competition being played back-to-back with the Western Rally, Tui said the demanding schedule did not affect their preparations.

item.title: Navatu embrace for historic finale
item.description: Navatu Secondary School’s under-19 rugby team and coaching staff visited Parliament yesterday as they continued preparations for their historic Vodafone Deans final against Lelean Memorial School this Saturday. The visit gave the Vanua Levu-based side an opportunity to step away from rugby before returning to training ahead of the biggest match of their campaign.
item.content:encoded:
Navatu Secondary School’s under-19 rugby team and coaching staff visited Parliament yesterday as they continued preparations for their historic Vodafone Deans final against Lelean Memorial School this Saturday.

The visit gave the Vanua Levu-based side an opportunity to step away from rugby before returning to training ahead of the biggest match of their campaign.

Navatu has battled through a demanding path to reach the final, overcoming some of the competition’s established teams along the way. Navatu defeated Queen Victoria School in the elimination round before overcoming Suva Grammar School in the quarter-final and Ratu Kadavulevu School in the semi-final.

Ravulo said the journey had tested the team at every stage but had also prepared the players for the challenge that awaits them. “This is a big experience for these boys who have come from Vanua Levu,” Ravulo said.

He said the team was using Monday as an opportunity to step away from rugby before returning to the field on today to begin final preparations.

Ravulo believes Navatu could be creating history as the first school from the North to reach this stage of the competition.

“Our journey this far has not been easy as we have met some giants of the Deans competition,” he said. Now, with Lelean standing between Navatu and the title, Ravulo has called on the school’s wider community to rally behind the team.

“I want to invite our supporters. I believe a good number are from the villages. They have returned yesterday and will come back on Thursday,” he said.

He also appealed to former students to get behind the team for what promises to be a major occasion for the school.

“At this stage of the competition, support is needed from those around Fiji and even the world, from all those who attended Navatu Secondary School,” Ravulo said.

“This is history for the ages. The boys are ready to do their part this week.”

Behind Navatu’s run has been strong support from parents, who Ravulo said have played a major role in keeping the team going throughout the campaign.

“What drives this team is the support of their parents. We don’t really have the financial backing. It is the parents who have been supporting us from Day One,” he said.

item.title: Schools football begins tomorrow
item.description: The wait is almost over, with the 2026 Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship set to kick off at Subrail Park in Labasa tomorrow. The four-day national championship will bring together 56 teams from across Fiji, with more than 1500 students, teachers and officials expected to converge on the North for the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
The wait is almost over, with the 2026 Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship set to kick off at Subrail Park in Labasa tomorrow.

The four-day national championship will bring together 56 teams from across Fiji, with more than 1500 students, teachers and officials expected to converge on the North for the tournament.

With national honours at stake, the opening day will provide teams with their first opportunity to lay down a marker in their respective grades.

The tournament will feature competition in the under-15, U17, U19 and girls categories, with schools determined to make a strong start to their campaigns.

The U19 competition will be particularly intriguing, with a new champion guaranteed after defending champions Tabia College failed to qualify.

The U17 title will also have a new winner, with defending champions Labasa College missing out.

Northern schools will be looking to make the most of home conditions, while teams from Viti Levu will be eager to challenge for national supremacy.

The action continues through Saturday, with the knockout stages scheduled for Friday before the finals on Saturday.
